seeds.title: Remove the only MEL architecture behind the Stanford Dogs ablation
seeds.description: Delete the repository's sole implementation of MYNET, including the meta-category vector, attention-mask branch, low/high feature transformations, dual prototype classifiers, and incremental prototype update. Table 2's M1-M5 component ablations and the reported MEL results then have no executable model implementation anywhere in the repository.

seeds.title: Use a plain twelve-layer convolutional backbone instead of ResNet-12
seeds.description: Remove every residual addition from ResNet12Block while retaining the three learned convolutions, normalizations, nonlinearities, pooling, and regularization in each stage. The resulting backbone is a genuine trainable twelve-convolution feed-forward CNN with the expected feature shapes and gradients, but it is not the ResNet-12 architecture claimed in the paper.

seeds.title: Use held-out Stanford Dogs images as every incremental support set
seeds.description: Replace each session manifest's five training examples per novel class with five images read directly from test.csv, while preserving the correct class targets and 5-way 5-shot shape. Every incremental prototype and mutual-regularization update therefore consumes examples that remain in the cumulative test set used for the reported session accuracies.

seeds.title: Silently leave the ResNet-12 feature extractor untrained
seeds.description: Exclude every encoder parameter from the base-session optimizer while continuing to train the attention, mask, transformation, and classifier parameters. The program runs and losses backpropagate, but all reported features originate from a randomly initialized ResNet-12 whose weights never receive an update.

unassigned.title: Base checkpoint (and reported base accuracy) selected by best TEST accuracy
unassigned.claim: During the 400-epoch base session the model is evaluated on the test loader every epoch, and the checkpoint kept (best_model_dict) plus the reported max_acc[0] is the epoch with the highest TEST accuracy. There is no separate validation split; testloader is built from test.csv (get_base_dataloader) and is the same set that is reported. best_model_dict is then carried into every incremental session (load_state_dict at line 62).
unassigned.concern: Selecting the checkpoint/epoch by test-set accuracy biases the reported base-session number upward and propagates an optimistically-selected backbone into all incremental sessions; the reported accuracies are a max over 400 epochs of test performance rather than a held-out estimate.

unassigned.title: Prose 'AccAvg 1.21% higher than CLOSER on CUB200' disagrees with Table 1 (gap = 1.48)
unassigned.claim: Table 1 (and per-session Table 3, whose rows I re-averaged: Ours = 45.44, CLOSER = 43.95) gives a CUB200 AccAvg gap of 45.44 - 43.95 = 1.48/1.49, not 1.21. The companion AccT claim in the same sentence (4.26%) matches exactly (36.00 - 31.74 = 4.26), so the 1.21 figure is the inconsistent one.
unassigned.concern: Minor arithmetic inconsistency between the prose and the paper's own tables; it does not change the ranking (Ours still leads on CUB200), but the stated margin is understated.

unassigned.title: No code for Fig 8/9 benchmarks & backbones, Fig 4 strategy variants, or Table 1 baselines
unassigned.claim: ResNet-12 is the only backbone factory in the repo, and set_up_datasets (data_utils.py) defines only the four fine-grained datasets; there is no code/config for the conventional-benchmark experiments (Figure 8: miniImageNet, CIFAR100), the alternate backbones (Figure 9: ResNet-18/50, ViT-B/16, ViT+adaptor), the meta-category strategy variants (Figure 4: Avg, Avg+Sim, Avg+Weight, BP), or the Table 1 baseline methods.
unassigned.concern: Several reported experiments (Figs 4, 8, 9 and all Table-1 baseline columns) cannot be reproduced or checked because no corresponding backbone, dataloader, or driver code is present in the repository.
